title: Show link emblem for all app launchers, not just the ones that are in fact symlinks to a file somewhere else
line: App launchers on the desktop and in Dolphin now always show the link emblem, not only when the file is a symlink.
explanation: KFileItem::overlays() only added emblem-symbolic-link when the file itself was a symlink, so a launcher symlinked from /usr/share/applications had the emblem while an identical copy (what Steam writes to ~/Desktop) looked like a plain file. For desktop files it only checked the Exec key to add the untrusted warning emblem. The change (Nate Graham's MR kio!1724, applied unchanged) adds the link emblem to every desktop file with an Exec key, once, and keeps the warning emblem for untrusted ones.

commits.message:
KFileItem: show the link emblem on all app launchers

Launchers only got the link emblem when the .desktop file happened to be
a symlink, so copies made by apps like Steam looked like plain files. Any
desktop file with an Exec key now gets the link emblem as well.

BUG: 493050

media.caption: Master: only the symlinked Kate (second) has the link emblem; the copied Kate and the Steam-style game launcher look like plain files
With the change: both Kate launchers and the Steam game show the link emblem (one each); the Type=Link web shortcut and the text file are unchanged
A non-executable (untrusted) launcher keeps the warning emblem next to the new link emblem

reviews.text: Clean, minimal fix in the right layer (KFileItem::overlays() in KIO) that adds emblem-symbolic-link to any readable local desktop file with an Exec key while avoiding duplicates on symlinks and preserving emblem-important for untrusted launchers. Matches Nate's design in comment 7 and kio!1724, and the before/after screenshots clearly verify copied launchers, symlinked launchers, Steam-style launchers, untrusted launchers, URL shortcuts, and plain files.

Implements exactly what Nate settled on in c5/c7: any desktop file with an Exec key gets emblem-symbolic-link, without doubling it for real symlinks, and the untrusted warning emblem is kept. KFileItem::overlays in KIO is the right layer (Folder View and Dolphin both use it), it reuses the KDesktopFile that was already parsed, and the screenshots show copied, symlinked and Steam-style launchers all getting a single emblem, while Type=Link and plain files are unchanged. Side effect worth knowing: every launcher in Dolphin (e.g. /usr/share/applications, ~/.config/autostart) now also shows the emblem, which fits the 'all app launchers' wording. Nit: since the code is Nate's kio!1724 unchanged, the commit should credit him as author rather than presenting it as new work.
